_comment: Per-artwork artist corrections, keyed by objectKey (folder/filename, NFC-normalised). Applied by build-data.mjs BEFORE the artists-db lookup, so a corrected name still picks up curated movement/nationality/dates. A null value clears the artist so the work falls into the anonymous bucket - used when the Commons `artist` field names only the uploader/photographer of the reproduction and the underlying creator is genuinely unrecorded. Never guess an attribution to fill a hole: every entry below cites the Commons evidence it came from. Regenerate data with `pnpm assets:build-data` after editing.

_why.collection-of-beauty/\"Le_jardin_Hosched: Commons categories: "1881 paintings by Alfred Sisley"; "dalbera" is uploader Jean-Pierre Dalbera (photo of the painting at Fondation Vuitton).
_why.collection-of-beauty/Henri_Rousseau_—_Th: Commons category "Paintings by Henri Rousseau"; "Gsimonov" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Holbein_—_Dead_Chri: Commons category "The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb (Holbein der Jungere)"; "Gsimonov" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Isenheim_Altarpiece: Commons category "Isenheim Altarpiece"; matches the three sibling panels already attributed to Grunewald. "Gsimonov" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Die-kreuzabnahme-ru: Commons category "The Descent from the Cross by Peter Paul Rubens (Siegerlandmuseum)" + PD-Art reproduction tag; "Illufant" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Claude_Monet-Soleil: Commons categories "1883 paintings", "Paintings of Etretat by Claude Monet"; "Ji-Elle" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/La_caída_de_Faetón_: Commons category "Formerly attributed to Jan Carel van Eyck" and the file page notes van Eyck "cannot have painted this as he was not born yet". Current attribution unresolved - left anonymous rather than guessed. "Jl FilpoC" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/PM_147978_B_Tournai: Commons category "La pointe du Cap Martin by Claude Monet"; "PMRMaeyaert" is uploader Paul M.R. Maeyaert.
_why.collection-of-beauty/The_Devil's_Bridge,: Commons categories "Paintings of the Alps by Joseph Mallord William Turner", "Paintings by Joseph Mallord William Turner in the Kunsthaus Zurich"; "Andrewrabbott" is the uploader.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Мавзолей_Шах-и-Зинд: A 2018 self-published photograph of the Shah-i-Zinda mausoleum ensemble - architecture, not a reproduced artwork. "Akhemen" is the photographer, so there is no artwork creator to record.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Carl_Spitzweg_-_Im_: Commons category "Paintings by Carl Spitzweg"; "Jean-Marc Pascolo" is the uploader who photographed it.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Giorgione-BildnisGi: Commons category "Portraits by Giorgione"; the file page credits the Bayerische Staatsgemaldesammlungen as the holding institution, not the painter.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Chaumiére_Italienne: Commons categories "Prints by Jean-Honore Fragonard", "1775 etchings"; file description: "Ets gemaakt door Jean-Honore Fragonard".
Commons category "Marriage at Cana (Paulo Veronese)" + PD-Art (Yorck Project); only the reproducing photographer was unknown.
_why.collection-of-beauty/Michelangelo_libyan: File description: "MICHELANGELO Buonarroti Study for the Libyan Sibyl"; Commons category "Drawings by Michelangelo Buonarroti in the Metropolitan Museum of Art".
_why.collection-of-beauty/El_Tres_de_Mayo,_by: Commons `artist` field is the derivative-work credit block verbatim: "El_Tres_de_Mayo,_by_Francisco_de_Goya,_from_Prado_in_Google_Earth.jpg : Francisco de Goya derivative work: Papa Lima Whiskey 2". "Papa Lima Whiskey 2" is the Commons user who cropped the black margin; the credit line confirms it ("This file was derived from: El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg"). The loose alias matcher used to rescue this by hitting "Goya" as a bare substring, and the record still resolves today only through the stale `artist_info` snapshot baked into the sidecar - a re-fetch under the strict matcher drops both, leaving the whole credit block as the artist name.
